name: Logroño (Spain)
description: White field with a dark red saltire reaching the corners of the cloth.
history: The flag of Logroño is rectangular, of proportions 2:3, white with a dark red saltire of a width equal to one sixth of the width of the flag reaching the corners of the cloth. The cross was granted by King Ferdinand III of Castile in 1237 for the help given by the people of Logroño in the taking of Baeza on 30 November 1227, Saint Andrew's day; the design with the cross of Saint Andrew is common in the Basque Country (Vitoria) and La Rioja and is also found in other lands that historically had a Spanish presence, such as the states of Florida and Alabama. There is documentary record of the old banner, and the city received honours from Isabella II on 6 December 1854 for the conduct of its inhabitants during the cholera epidemics.
